in_latin.name: Patrizia
in_latin.meaning: patricius femininus, forma feminina del cognomen patricius, indicante appartenenza a una famiglia nobilitata
in_latin.long_meaning: patricius femininus, forma feminina del cognomen patricius, indicante appartenenza a una famiglia nobilitata, nome originariamente utilizzato per indicare la discendenza da una famiglia aristocratica, da qui deriva il significato di 'nobile' e 'patrizio', nome molto comune nell'epoca medievale, ha una grande importanza nella tradizione cristiana per rappresentare la nobiltà spirituale

in_english.long_meaning: patrician, feminine form of patrician, signifying noble birth and belonging to a noble family, derived from the Latin 'patricius', meaning 'of or pertaining to a father' and 'of noble birth', with the feminine suffix to denote a female bearing the qualities of a noble and a father, a name highly significant in the Christian tradition for representing spiritual nobility and the dignity of Christ

historical_references.reference: Patrizia was a noblewoman and a member of the powerful Orsini family in medieval Italy. She was born in the late 13th century and was known for her beauty and intelligence. In 1325, she was married to Louis I, Duke of Anjou, who was a prominent figure in the European political scene. Their union was part of a larger political alliance between the Orsini and the Angevin dynasties.

Patrizia de' Medici was an Italian nun and abbess who lived in the 16th century. She was born into the powerful and influential Medici family, one of the most prominent in Renaissance Florence. Patrizia became a nun at a young age and later served as the abbess of the Santa Croce convent in Florence. She was known for her piety and her efforts to reform the convent.
